page_title: Hammerdeck — big screens, many screens, no dragging

summary.name: Hammerdeck
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native macOS window manager and automation app that puts grid placement, display throws/swaps, and a rules engine on keyboard hotkeys and chords.
use_cases: arrange windows on ultrawide or multi-display setups
send a window to another display with a keyboard shortcut
place windows into grid cells with one key
automatically rearrange windows when monitors connect
switch between windows across all apps
summary.what_it_does: Hammerdeck is a native Swift macOS app with an embedded Lua engine. Its window features include grid placement (a cell or a rectangle spanning several cells, with 3x3, 2x2, and 6-cell grids), throwing a window to the next display, swapping two displays' windows, and a Window Deck that tiles a screen's windows and enlarges the focused one. A Window Fan spreads windows against screen edges for switching, and Window Rewind undoes the most recent window move. A rules engine runs actions on signals like displays connecting, app launches, or appearance changes. Other included features cover a clipboard history, a Chrome/Safari tab switcher, quick site launching, break reminders, and a command palette. Logs are kept as local plain-text files.
notable: Throws windows between displays and swaps two displays' windows, which the page says macOS has no shortcut for
Rules engine lets you wire triggers like monitor connect to window layouts without writing code, with optional Lua extensions
Local MCP endpoint (off by default, loopback only) for coding agents to inspect and test extensions
Installable via Homebrew cask or disk image; signed and notarized by Apple
caveats: Several features need Accessibility permission; some need Automation, Screen Recording, or Full Disk Access granted manually
Text Actions' AI transforms require the user's own OpenAI key
Running from the disk image works but the app cannot update itself from there
